chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Dizzy and Ben Webster in Cab Calloway's band
summary: Dizzy and Ben, both with Cab Calloway, played with Collins at the Grampion Hotel, and Calloway's band stretched out occasionally.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You said at one point that you and Dizzy and Ben went to play together at Ben's hotel. Did you three ever record together?

No, we'd just play, and exchange ideas and chordally and otherwise. And Ben was living at the Grampion Hotel, and we would go -- they both at this time were with Cab Calloway, Ben and Dizzy, and it was -- we'd just sit there all day and just out of sheer enjoyment, you know, just play.
I know that Cab Calloway had some was a fan-tastically great musician with him.
Then did they get a chance to play a lot because I've seen like film shorts, and Calloway is mugging and singing, dancing and --
Carrying on (Unintelligible). You didn't see much of the band in performance, did the band stretch out?

Yeah, the band had a chance to stretch out occasionally, yeah, yeah. It was inevitable, hey, you couldn't keep those guys down but so long any way. Because at this time, let's see, I think J. C. Heard was the drummer, Hunter Henton --
